title: Emem language - Wikipedia
text: Emem, or Emumu, is an Eastern Pauwasi language in Keerom Regency, Papua Province. It has only 25% lexical similarity with Zorop, the most distinct Eastern Pauwasi language.

title: Pauwasi languages - Wikipedia
text: The Pauwasi languages are a likely family of Papuan languages, mostly in Indonesia. The best described Pauwasi language is Karkar, across the border in Papua New Guinea.

title: Emem language — Grokipedia
text: Emem, also known as Emumu, is an Eastern Pauwasi language of the Papuan (non-Austronesian) family, spoken by approximately 2,000 native speakers in five remote villages—Yuruf, Umuaf (or Mofon), Yambraf Satu, Yambraf Dua (or Embi), and Semografi—in the mountainous Web Subdistrict of Keerom Regency, northeastern Papua Province, Indonesia. title: East Pauwasi languages — Grokipedia
text: The East Pauwasi language family includes three primary member languages: Zorop, Emem, and Karkar-Yuri, which together form a genetic subgroup characterized by lexical and structural affinities within the Pauwasi family across the border between Papua Province, Indonesia, and Sandaun Province, Papua New Guinea.
